newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cent higher Thursday, dealers said.

Wednesday, New York arabica futures ended up sharply, with spot May soaring to a 2-1/2-year high amid continued concern about the amount of available supplies for roasters this year. May delivery closed at 208.05 cents a lb, up 15.65 cents, after trading from 213 to 203. July surged 10.65 cents to 185.30 cents.
The May/July switch grew to 22.75 cents from 17.75 cents at the close on Tuesday.

Sparking the rally was a monthly report issued by the Green Coffee Association of New York late Tuesday, which showed that supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose in March by only 111,000 132-pound bags to a total 1,657,000 bags.

Most analysts had forecast a rise of between 250,000 and 300,000 bags, with some looking for a build-up of supplies of as much as 700,000 bags due to stepped-up shipments from Latin America in recent weeks to cash in on higher prices.
Technically, traders pegged May resistance at Wednesday's high of 213.00 cents, with the next upside objective near 220.00. Support was seen at 205.00 cents, then 200.00 cents.
Brazil's two key coffee ports after Santos are expected to be hit by a 48-hour national strike by stevedores due to begin at 0700 local/1000 GMT Friday, unions said.
Union officials in Rio de Janeiro and Vitoria said Wednesday they would participate in the national strike, the second in two weeks following a 24-hour stoppage on April 4.
London robusta prices firmed across the board by the midday break Thursday, but profit-taking blunted gains. LIFFE May stood $20 higher at $1,630 a tonne.
